Tewahedo baptismal-catechesis cites Gen 2:7 + Jn 20:22 as the protological-Pentecostal-pair anchoring image-restoration in the Spirit.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, De Incarnatione Verbi (On the Incarnation), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 25 (1857).

entries.summary: 'And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel' — Athanasius marks tou spermatos autēs (HER seed, singular feminine-genitive) as the PROTEVANGELIUM-anchor: the unique-feminine-genitive sperma points to the Virgin's-seed (Mary alone among women conceives without male-seed) and so to the Word-incarnate as the prophesied head-bruiser of the serpent. Athanasius pairs Gen 3:15 with Isa 7:14 (almah-parthenos) and Gal 4:4 (genomenon ek gynaikos — 'born of a woman') as the canonical-virginal-conception triplet. Tewahedo Marian-theology preserves the Eve / New-Eve typology directly from this Genesis-protevangelium reading.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, De Incarnatione Verbi (On the Incarnation), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 25 (1857).

entries.summary: 'And Melchizedek king of Salem brought forth bread and wine: and he was the priest of the most high God' — Athanasius marks the Melchizedek-priesthood as the PRE-INCARNATIONAL christophany / typological-shadow of the eternal-high-priesthood the Word exercises post-incarnation per Heb 7. The priest hiereus tou theou tou hypsistou (priest of God Most High) and the bread-and-wine offering both prefigure the Word's-Eucharistic-priesthood. Heb 7:3's 'without father, without mother, without descent' — Athanasius reads not of Melchizedek-the-man but of Melchizedek-the-type / the Word he prefigures: only the eternal-Son is literally without-descent (anepidektos genealogias). Tewahedo Anaphora liturgy preserves the Melchizedek-Christ priestly-typology at the bread-and-wine offering.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'And in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed' — Athanasius marks en tō spermati sou (in thy seed, singular) as the ABRAHAMIC-SEED-AS-CHRIST anchor — explicitly so-interpreted by Paul at Gal 3:16 (ou legei kai tois spermasin... all' hōs eph' henos, kai tō spermati sou, hos estin Christos — 'he saith not and to seeds, as of many, but of one, and to thy seed, which is Christ'). The singular-not-plural sperma is the exegetical-key: the Abrahamic-blessing-to-all-nations is fulfilled in the one-Word-incarnate, not in Abraham's biological-descendants per se. Athanasius pairs Gen 22:18 with the Magi-narrative (Mt 2:1-12) and Acts 3:25 as the canonical Abrahamic-blessing-of-all-nations fulfillment-triplet.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'And the Lord said unto Moses, See, I have made thee a god to Pharaoh: and Aaron thy brother shall be thy prophet' — Athanasius marks dedōka se theon tō Pharaō (I have given thee as a god to Pharaoh) as the METHODOLOGICAL-KEY for the gods-by-participation vs theotēs-by-nature distinction. Moses is called 'god' by ECONOMIC-COMMUNICATION (his role-as-divine-mediator to Pharaoh) and by DIVINE-GRACIOUS-GRANT, not by nature. The Word, by contrast, is God by-nature (kata physin), not by-grace (kata charin); is-eternally-God, not-made-god. Athanasius pairs Exo 7:1 with Psa 82:6 ('I have said, Ye are gods'; cf. Jn 10:34) as the canonical-theōsis-by-grace pair, contrasting both with the Son's-deity-by-essence. Crucial anti-Arian hermeneutical-grid.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'And he said, Thou canst not see my face: for there shall no man see me, and live' — Athanasius marks ou dynēsē idein mou to prosōpon (thou canst not see my face) as the UNSEEABLE-FATHER / VISIBLE-WORD distinction. The Father-in-his-essence is unseeable (1 Tim 6:16 oude idein tis dynatai); what Moses is granted to see (LXX ta opisthia — 'the back parts') is the visible-condescension of the Word-pre-incarnate. Athanasius reads the Word as the agent of EVERY OT theophany (the burning bush, the pillar of cloud, the man-Yahweh at Mamre, the Sinai-glory) — the Father is never seen, only the Word who is the Father's-form-and-image. This hermeneutic grounds the Tewahedo iconographic-convention: the Father is never directly-depicted, only the Word-incarnate.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'For thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption' (LXX 15:10 — ouk enkataleipseis tēn psychēn mou eis hadēn, oude dōseis ton hosion sou idein diaphthoran) — Athanasius marks Ps 16:10 as the DEFINITIVE RESURRECTION-PROOFTEXT, citing Peter's exposition (Acts 2:25-31) and Paul's (Acts 13:35-37) as canonical-apostolic exegesis: the verse cannot be of David (whose tomb remains) but must be of David's-greater-Son, the Word-incarnate, whose flesh in the tomb did-not-see-corruption (idein diaphthoran) because the deathless-Word remained-united-to-it even through the three-day-pause. The non-corruption of the dead-flesh-of-Christ is the soteriological-key: by-Word's-presence-in-it, death itself is decomposed-from-within. Tewahedo Holy-Saturday liturgy cites Ps 16:10 + Acts 2:27 as the harrowing-of-Hades-anchor-pair.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, De Incarnatione Verbi (On the Incarnation), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 25 (1857).

entries.summary: 'My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?' (LXX 21:2 — ho theos ho theos mou, prosches moi, hina ti enkatelipes me) — Athanasius marks the CRY-OF-DERELICTION as voiced-by-the-assumed-flesh, NOT by the divine-Word as such. The divine-Word cannot be forsaken by the Father (Jn 16:32 — kai ouk eimi monos, hoti ho Patēr met' emou estin — 'and I am not alone, for the Father is with me'); the Word remains-eternally-with-the-Father even through the cross. The cry is voiced by the Word-IN-the-flesh, redeeming-from-within the human-experience of God-forsakenness. This anti-patripassian reading is CONSTITUTIVE for Tewahedo Holy-Friday Trisagion: 'Holy God who was crucified FOR US' — qua-flesh-suffered, qua-Word-impassible.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: the sceptre of thy kingdom is a right sceptre' (LXX 44:7 — ho thronos sou ho theos eis ton aiōna tou aiōnos) — Athanasius marks Ps 45:6 (LXX 44:7) as the DIRECT VOCATIVE-ADDRESS of the Son as ho theos (the-God, with definite article). The Father is the speaker; the Son the addressee; the address is unambiguous in the vocative-with-article. The author of Hebrews (1:8) cites this verse against the angels — 'unto which of the angels said he at any time...' (1:5) and culminates with this 'But unto the Son he saith, Thy throne, O God' — Athanasius treats Heb 1:8's citation as the canonical apostolic-warrant for reading Ps 45:6's vocative as direct-Trinitarian-address, not metaphor or hypostatized-attribute.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High' (LXX 81:6 — egō eipa theoi este kai huioi hypsistou pantes) — Athanasius marks Ps 82:6 as the THEŌSIS-BY-GRACE anchor — explicitly cited by the Word himself at Jn 10:34-35 to silence the blasphemy-charge for his ego eimi self-identification. The human-recipients of the divine-word are called 'gods' by-participation, by-grace, by-econoomic-divine-naming; the Word is God by-nature, by-essence, by-eternal-generation. Athanasius's signature theōsis-formula in DI §54 — 'He was made man that we might be made God' (autos enēnthrōpēsen hina hēmeis theopoiēthōmen) — rests on this Ps 82:6 / Exo 7:1 / 2 Pet 1:4 grammar: gods-by-grace through-the-Word who-is-God-by-nature. The Tewahedo soteriology preserves this asymmetric grammar at every catechetical level.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, or ever the earth was' (LXX 8:23 — pro tou aiōnos ethemeliōsen me en archē) — Athanasius marks pro tou aiōnos (before the age) as the exegetical-extension of his Pr 8:22 ektisen-me reading: the ethemeliōsen me ('he founded/established me') refers NOT to Wisdom's-coming-into-being but to Wisdom's ECONOMIC-FOUNDATION / pre-temporal-mission. The Word is appointed-to-his-incarnational-task before-the-foundation-of-the-world (1 Pet 1:20), but his being-the-Word is uncreated-and-eternal. Athanasius pairs Pr 8:23 with Eph 1:4 (proegnōsmenou pro katabolēs kosmou) as the canonical pre-temporal-economic-mission-foundation pair.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'Then I was by him, as one brought up with him' (LXX 8:30 — ēmēn par' autō harmozousa) — Athanasius marks harmozousa (a harmoniser/fitter-together; cf. some MSS architechtonousa, a master-architect/master-builder) as the WISDOM-AS-CO-CREATIONAL-AGENT anchor: Wisdom is not the Father's-instrument-from-outside but intra-divine co-architect, harmonising-all-things from within the divine-counsel. The text par' autō (BY him, beside him) positions Wisdom as eternal-companion-of-the-Father, not posterior-creature. Pairs with Jn 1:3 (panta di' autou egeneto — 'all things were made through him') as the canonical Wisdom-as-Trinitarian-creator pair.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief' — Athanasius marks Isa 53:3-5 as the MOST-EXPLICIT prophetic-anchor of the Suffering-Servant theology the Word-incarnate fulfills. The despising-and-rejection are borne by the assumed-humanity (Word-IN-the-flesh tasting human rejection on behalf of all-the-rejected); the bearing-of-griefs (LXX houtos tas hamartias hēmōn pherei) is the substitutionary-atonement-mechanism. The Word's-impassible-divinity is preserved (the Word-qua-Word cannot suffer); the assumed-flesh truly-suffers, and the suffering is salvifically-imputed to the Word's-Person. Pairs with 1 Pet 2:24 (hos tas hamartias hēmōn autos anēnenken en tō sōmati autou epi to xylon) as the canonical Suffering-Servant-fulfilled-in-Christ pair.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, De Incarnatione Verbi (On the Incarnation), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 25 (1857).

entries.summary: 'The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me; because the LORD hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek' — Athanasius marks Pneuma kyriou ep' eme (the Spirit of the Lord upon me) as the PARADIGMATIC communicatio-idiomatum anchor for pneumatology: the Word, qua-his-assumed-humanity, RECEIVES the Spirit (anointed-as-prophet/Messiah, with-the-Spirit, fulfilled at the Jordan-baptism); the Word, qua-his-divinity, SENDS the Spirit (the Pentecost-outpouring, the John-20:22 in-breathing). The Word is simultaneously Spirit-recipient (qua-flesh) and Spirit-sender (qua-Word). Christ-himself at the Nazareth-synagogue (Lk 4:18) applies this verse to himself: sēmeron peplērōtai hē graphē hautē — 'today this scripture is fulfilled.' The Tewahedo epiclesis-of-the-Spirit in the Anaphora rests on this dual-Spirit-economy: the Word who-receives-and-sends the Spirit is the same Word the priestly-prayer invokes.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Epistulae ad Serapionem de Spiritu Sancto (Letters to Serapion on the Holy Spirit, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857). The Serapion correspondence is Athanasius's principal anti-pneumatomachian work, refuting the Tropici denial of the Holy Spirit's divinity and homoousion with Father + Son.

entries.summary: 'And lo a voice from heaven, saying, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased' — Athanasius marks the JORDAN-BAPTISMAL-THEOPHANY as the FIRST-EXPLICIT Trinitarian self-disclosure of the New Covenant: the Father's-voice from heaven + the Son in the water + the Spirit visibly-descending as dove. The three Persons are simultaneously-disclosed in one-economic-event. Athanasius reads this disclosure as the pedagogical-foundation for the Mt 28:19 baptismal-formula commanded at the end of the same Gospel: what was disclosed at Christ's-baptism becomes the pattern-of-Christian-initiation. The Tewahedo Epiphany-feast (Timkat) liturgically re-enacts this Trinitarian-baptismal-theophany annually as the most-public Tewahedo solemnity.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Epistulae ad Serapionem de Spiritu Sancto (Letters to Serapion on the Holy Spirit, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857). The Serapion correspondence is Athanasius's principal anti-pneumatomachian work, refuting the Tropici denial of the Holy Spirit's divinity and homoousion with Father + Son.

entries.summary: 'And Simon Peter answered and said, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God' — Athanasius marks Peter's confession as FATHER-REVEALED (per the immediately-following v. 17 — sarx kai haima ouk apekalypsen soi, all' ho Patēr mou — 'flesh and blood did not reveal it to thee, but my Father'). The confession articulates the homoousion-of-the-Son before-Nicaea-articulates-it-lexically: Son-of-the-LIVING-God positions the Son as sharing the LIFE-by-essence of the Father (the auto-zōē), not as having received-life from outside. The Father's-revelation-of-this-truth is itself trinitarian: the Father reveals the Son's homoousion BY the Spirit to Peter, foreshadowing 1 Cor 12:3 (no one says kyrios Iēsous except by Holy Spirit).
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt' — Athanasius marks the GETHSEMANE-PRAYER as voiced-by-the-assumed-flesh in its natural-creaturely-recoil from death, not by the divine-Word as such. The divine-Word's-will is identical to the Father's-will (Jn 5:30, 8:29); only the assumed-flesh prays the parelthetō to potērion (let the cup pass). The plēn ouch hōs egō thelō all' hōs sy (nevertheless not as I will but as thou) demonstrates the OBEDIENCE of the assumed-flesh subordinating-itself to the divine-economic-will. Crucial against Apollinarian-reduction of Christ's human-soul: only a true-human-soul can pray as-creature.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'And about the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is to say, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?' — Athanasius marks the cross-cry as DIRECT Ps 22:1 fulfillment in the assumed-flesh. The Word is not actually-forsaken (Jn 16:32 — 'the Father is with me'); the Word voices THROUGH the assumed-flesh the human-experience of God-forsakenness, redeeming-that-experience from within. The Aramaic preservation of the cry (Eli Eli) marks it as Jesus's-actual-speech, transmitted-untranslated by the Gospel tradition — the rawness of the dereliction-cry is preserved liturgically. Tewahedo Holy-Friday Trisagion ('Holy God who was crucified FOR US') sets the impassibility-paradox at the cross's-cry directly.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, De Incarnatione Verbi (On the Incarnation), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 25 (1857).

entries.summary: 'The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God' — Athanasius marks the Markan-incipit as the gospel-condensed: archē tou euangeliou Iēsou Christou huiou theou. The Son-of-God title in the incipit is NON-ADOPTIVE — not 'became Son at baptism' (per the immediately-following baptismal-narrative, which discloses-not-confers the sonship) — but constitutive-of-the-gospel-Jesus's-identity from the gospel's first sentence. Athanasius pairs Mk 1:1 with Jn 1:1-14 as the canonical constitutive-not-adoptive-sonship gospel-anchor. Mark's-immediacy (no birth-narrative, no genealogy) makes the constitutive-claim MORE pointed: the gospel-of-the-Son-of-God begins-as-already-being-the-gospel-of-the-Son-of-God, with no developmental-arc-toward-sonship.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'But of that day and that hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels which are in heaven, neither the Son, but the Father' — Athanasius engages this verse extensively (CA III.42-50, an entire mini-treatise) as the CRUCIAL ARIAN PROOFTEXT. His resolution: 'the Son knoweth not' is voiced QUA-flesh, QUA-economic-pedagogy, NOT qua-divine-Logos (who knows-all-things per Jn 16:30, 21:17 — sy panta oidas). The Word who-is-the-Father's-Wisdom cannot be ignorant; what the assumed-flesh-as-flesh does-not-know-by-its-natural-limits is what is here predicated of 'the Son' in his human-economy. Pedagogically, the not-knowing is salutary for the disciples (it prevents idle-eschatological-speculation and enforces vigilance per the same chapter's grēgoreite). Tewahedo eschatological-piety preserves this Athanasian both/and: the Son-qua-divinity knows-all-times, the Son-qua-assumed-flesh models-the-watchful-not-knowing.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'And Jesus said, I am: and ye shall see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power, and coming in the clouds of heaven' — Athanasius marks egō eimi (I AM) as Christ's-self-identification with the Exodus 3:14 divine-Name (egō eimi ho ōn LXX) at the moment-of-his-passion-confession before Caiaphas. Paired with kathēmenon ek dexiōn tēs dynameōs (sitting at the right-hand-of-power) the saying chains Ps 110:1 right-hand-of-power-exaltation + Dan 7:13 Son-of-man-coming-with-clouds + the I-AM divine-Name in one tripartite-Christological-confession. Athanasius marks this as the CLIMACTIC public-self-disclosure of the Word's-deity: Mark's-Jesus discloses-himself most explicitly precisely-at-the-moment of being-condemned for blasphemy (the unjustness of the condemnation rests on the truth of the I-AM).
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God' — Athanasius marks the ANNUNCIATION as the PRINCIPAL TRINITARIAN-INCARNATIONAL-MOMENT: the Spirit (Pneuma Hagion) comes-upon the Virgin to prepare-and-sanctify her flesh as worthy-temple; the dynamis tou Hypsistou (power of the Highest) is the divine-Logos who is conceived-in-her; the Hypsistos (the Highest = the Father) is the sending-source. All three Persons are active in the single Annunciation-event. The episkiasei (overshadow) verb echoes the Shekinah-cloud overshadowing the tabernacle (Exo 40:34-38 LXX) — Mary becomes the new tabernacle of the Word's-glorious-presence. Tewahedo Marian-theology (Kidana Mahrat, the Covenant of Mercy) rests on this Annunciation-Trinitarian-overshadowing-Theotokos-ecclesia anchor.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Epistulae ad Serapionem de Spiritu Sancto (Letters to Serapion on the Holy Spirit, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857). The Serapion correspondence is Athanasius's principal anti-pneumatomachian work, refuting the Tropici denial of the Holy Spirit's divinity and homoousion with Father + Son.

entries.summary: 'And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man' — Athanasius marks proekopten sophia kai hēlikia (he advanced in wisdom and stature) as a QUA-FLESH developmental-increase, NOT a qua-Word increase-in-wisdom (the Word is the Father's-Wisdom by-essence and cannot become-wiser). The advancement names the assumed-flesh's-real-growth: an infant-Word grows into a young-Word; a young-Word learns the carpenter's-trade; the developmentally-real human-experience is genuinely-experienced by the Word-incarnate without compromising the Word's-eternal-perfection-in-knowledge. Crucial anti-Docetic and anti-Apollinarian text: Christ's-humanity is developmentally-genuine, not pre-formed-or-shortcut. Tewahedo Christology preserves this developmental-realism in its catechesis of the child-Jesus's growth.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'No man knoweth who the Son is, but the Father; and who the Father is, but the Son, and he to whom the Son will reveal him' — Athanasius marks Lk 10:22 as the LUKAN-PARALLEL of Mt 11:27 (treated already in γ.4.9 seed) — the MUTUAL-KNOWLEDGE-FORMULA as homoousion-prooftext. The Lukan-form's variation (oudeis ginōskei tis estin ho huios ei mē ho Patēr — 'no one knoweth WHO the Son is') emphasizes the WHO-question: the Son's-identity is known exhaustively-only-by-the-Father, and reciprocally. Only-equals-by-nature exhaustively-know-each-other (a creature could not exhaustively-know the Father). The exhaustive-mutual-knowledge therefore-requires homoousion. Pairs with Mt 11:27 as the canonical-synoptic mutual-knowledge-homoousion pair.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made' — Athanasius marks panta di' autou egeneto, kai chōris autou egeneto oude hen ho gegonen (all-things came-into-being THROUGH him, and apart-from-him came-into-being not-one-thing of-what-came-into-being) as the CREATIONAL-ASYMMETRY anchor against Arian inclusion-of-the-Son-in-creation. The Word is the THROUGH-WHOM-of-creation (di' autou), not part-of-what-came-into-being. The repeated egeneto / egeneto / gegonen (came-into-being) applies to creation-creatures, NEVER to the Word (Jn 1:1 — ēn ho Logos, was-the-Word, imperfect-tense-eternal-being, contrasts with egeneto came-into-being). The grammatical-distinction is decisive: the Word is, all-other-things came-to-be.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'That all men should honour the Son, even as they honour the Father. He that honoureth not the Son honoureth not the Father which hath sent him' — Athanasius marks hina pantes timōsi ton Huion kathōs timōsi ton Patera (that all should honor the Son EVEN AS they honor the Father) as the HOMOTĪMION (equal-honor) prooftext. Equal-honor is owed-by-creatures only to one equal-in-nature (homoousios) with the Father; therefore the kathōs (EVEN AS, in-the-same-manner-as) directly entails homoousion. Any reduction of the Son to creature-status would make this equal-honor idolatrous; the Word's-own-claim therefore-positively-requires divine-essence. Pairs with Phil 2:10 (every-knee-shall-bow at-the-name-of-Jesus) as the canonical equal-divine-worship pair.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'Ye have heard how I said unto you, I go away, and come again unto you. If ye loved me, ye would rejoice, because I said, I go unto the Father: for my Father is greater than I' — Athanasius marks ho Patēr meizōn mou estin (the Father is greater than I) as the HARDEST ARIAN PROOFTEXT, addressed extensively at CA I.58-64. His resolution: 'greater' (meizōn) names the Father's-being-the-source / fount-of-deity (the unbegotten-pēgē, ho agennētos), while the Son is the begotten-from-Father (gegennēmenos ek tou Patros). The greater-than is RELATIONAL-ORIGIN, not substantial-inequality. The same-essence is communicated entirely-from-Father-to-Son; the Father is greater in the order-of-origination, not in the order-of-being. Pairs with Jn 10:30 (egō kai ho Patēr hen esmen — one in essence) as the canonical-Cappadocian-Athanasian source-without-subordination pair.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'And now, O Father, glorify thou me with thine own self with the glory which I had with thee before the world was' — Athanasius marks tē doxē hē eichon pro tou ton kosmon einai para soi (the glory which I HAD with thee BEFORE the world was) as the DECISIVE pre-temporal-co-glory anchor: the Word's-glory is shared-with-the-Father before-the-cosmos-existed. Any creaturely glory-by-grace would be post-temporal (since creatures begin-to-be in time); only the Word, eternally-co-existent with the Father, can claim pre-temporal-shared-glory. The eichon (imperfect-tense, continuous-prior-state) excludes any 'gradually-acquired' Arian reading. Pairs with Jn 1:1 (en archē ēn ho Logos, kai ho Logos ēn pros ton theon) as the canonical pre-temporal-co-existence pair. The Tewahedo Doxology preserves this pre-temporal-glory in the Gloria-Patri-pattern: 'as it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be.'
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'Being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God, which liveth and abideth for ever' — Athanasius marks dia logou zōntos theou kai menontos (through the living-and-abiding word of God) as ambiguating-favorably-toward-Christology: the divine-Logos himself effects the regeneration through whom the scriptural-logos and the Spirit-of-Christ co-act. The incorruptible-seed (sporas aphthartos) is the Word's-life-communicated; the new-birth is Christic-incorporation. Athanasius pairs 1Pe 1:23 with Jn 3:5 (water-and-Spirit re-birth) and Jas 1:18 (he-of-his-own-will brought-us-forth by-the-word-of-truth) as the canonical regeneration-by-Word-and-Spirit triplet. Theōsis-grammar requires this regeneration-prerequisite: only the new-born can be deified.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, De Incarnatione Verbi (On the Incarnation), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 25 (1857).

entries.summary: 'For even hereunto were ye called: because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps' — Athanasius marks Christos epathen hyper hymōn (Christ suffered for us) as the SOTERIOLOGICAL-PARADIGMATIC pair: the suffering is BOTH substitutionary (hyper hymōn — on-your-behalf, in-your-place) AND paradigmatic (hypogrammon — a writing-pattern-to-copy). Christ's-suffering simultaneously redeems and exemplifies; the soteriological efficacy makes the moral-imitation possible rather than mere-moralism. The Word qua-divine cannot suffer; the Word qua-assumed-flesh genuinely-suffers and the suffering is salvifically-imputed to the Word's-Person. Pairs with 1 Pet 3:18 (Christ once-suffered for sins) as the canonical-substitutionary-Petrine-pair.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'By which also he went and preached unto the spirits in prison; Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah' — Athanasius marks tois en phylakē pneumasin poreutheis ekēryxen (the spirits in prison having-gone he-preached-to-them) as the HARROWING-OF-HADES anchor: the Word's-soul (united-to-the-Word's-divinity even through the three-day-burial-pause) travels to release the OT-righteous (and to confront the OT-disobedient — the antediluvian-spirits) in the inter-mortem state. The Word does NOT release-himself from the body (the Word remains-united-to-flesh even in the tomb); rather, the unified-Christ-in-his-soul descends-to-Hades while-the-body-rests-in-the-tomb. The harrowing is the inaugural-moment of the Word's-Paschal-Cosmic-Victory. Tewahedo Holy-Saturday iconography (Anastasis-icon: Christ pulling Adam + Eve out of the tomb) preserves this 1 Peter 3:19-anchored harrowing-tradition.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, De Incarnatione Verbi (On the Incarnation), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 25 (1857).

entries.summary: 'According as his divine power hath given unto us all things that pertain unto life and godliness, through the knowledge of him that hath called us to glory and virtue' — Athanasius marks tēs theias dynameōs autou (his divine-power) as the PNEUMATOLOGICAL EXTENSION of the 2 Pet 1:4 theōsis-grant (γ.4.9 seed anchor). The divine-power that grants life-and-godliness IS the Spirit-of-Christ; the gifts pertain to the Spirit's-economy IN-the-believer. Athanasius reads ta pros zōēn kai eusebeian (the-things-for-life-and-godliness) as the totality-of-the-Spirit's-fruits which PREPARE the believer-for-theōsis. Pairs with 2 Pet 1:4 (partakers-of-the-divine-nature) as the canonical Petrine pneumatological-theōsis pair, both grounded in the divine-power of the One who-called-us.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Epistulae ad Serapionem de Spiritu Sancto (Letters to Serapion on the Holy Spirit, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857). The Serapion correspondence is Athanasius's principal anti-pneumatomachian work, refuting the Tropici denial of the Holy Spirit's divinity and homoousion with Father + Son.

entries.summary: 'But grow in grace, and in the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ. To him be glory both now and for ever. Amen' — Athanasius marks autō hē doxa nyn kai eis hēmeran aiōnos (to HIM be the glory now and unto the day of eternity) as a DOXOLOGICAL-WORSHIP-OF-CHRIST anchor that the Arians cannot consistently maintain. The doxa-directed-to-Christ is the creature's-worship-act that is owed to God-by-nature alone (the first-commandment exclusion of creature-worship). If Christ were a creature-by-nature, this doxology would be idolatrous; the verse's own-internal-logic-positively-requires Christ's-divine-essence. Pairs with 2 Pet 3:18 with Rev 1:6 (autō hē doxa kai to kratos eis tous aiōnas) and Rev 5:13 (autō hē doxa kai hē timē) as the canonical worship-directed-to-Christ Apocalyptic-Petrine triplet.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'He that committeth sin is of the devil; for the devil sinneth from the beginning. For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil' — Athanasius marks eis touto ephanerōthē ho Huios tou theou hina lysē ta erga tou diabolou (for THIS purpose was-manifested the Son-of-God, that he might LOOSEN-DOWN/DESTROY the works of the devil) as the SOTERIOLOGICAL-PURPOSE-STATEMENT of the Incarnation. The ephanerōthē (was-manifested) is the technical-incarnational verb — the eternal-Word-who-IS becomes-visibly-manifest in flesh-and-action. The hina-purpose clause names the polemical-redemptive-telos: not abstractly 'salvation' but specifically destroying-the-works-of-the-devil — sin, death, deception, the cosmic-tyrant. Pairs with Heb 2:14 (hina dia tou thanatou katargēsē ton to kratos echonta tou thanatou, tout' estin ton diabolon — that through-death he-might-destroy the one having the power-of-death, that is, the devil) as the canonical-incarnational-destroying-the-devil pair.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, De Incarnatione Verbi (On the Incarnation), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 25 (1857).

entries.summary: 'Hereby know ye the Spirit of God: Every spirit that confesseth that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is of God' — Athanasius marks Iēsoun Christon en sarki elēlythota (Jesus Christ in-flesh having-come) as the FOUNDATIONAL ANTI-DOCETIC CREEDAL FORMULA. The en sarki (in-flesh) is non-negotiable: the genuine-fleshly-advent of the Word excludes Docetic phantasm-Christology and Apollinarian rationalist-Christology alike. The Letter to Epictetus addresses precisely this controversy in Athanasius's own era: certain Egyptian-Christians had argued that the Word's-flesh was homoousios with the Word's-divinity (a kind of Apollinarian-reductionism in reverse). Athanasius vigorously denies this: the Word's-flesh is genuine-Mary-derived-human-flesh, NOT a divine-derivative; the Word is-from-the-Father, the flesh is-from-the-Virgin.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Epistola ad Epictetum (Letter to Epictetus, Bishop of Corinth), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD.

entries.summary: 'In this was manifested the love of God toward us, because that God sent his only begotten Son into the world, that we might live through him' — Athanasius marks ton Huion autou ton monogenē (his ONLY-BEGOTTEN Son) as the UNIQUE-GENERATION anchor: monogenēs names the Son as uniquely-from-the-Father's-essence (monos-genos = of-one-kind / of-the-same-kind-as-the-Father-alone), distinct from any creature's-coming-into-being. The Latin tradition translates as unigenitus (only-begotten); the Greek monogenēs is more-precisely 'unique-of-his-kind.' The uniqueness excludes creature-categorization (the Son is NOT first-among-many-creatures) and the begotten-genos excludes the Spirit-pneumatomachian reduction (the Son's-generation is from-Father-essence, not creaturely-act). Pairs with Jn 1:18 (monogenēs theos — the only-begotten-God) and Jn 3:16 as the canonical monogenēs Christological-trio.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore, Amen; and have the keys of hell and of death' — Athanasius marks egō eimi ho zōn, kai egenomēn nekros, kai idou zōn eimi eis tous aiōnas (I-AM the-living-one, and I-became dead, and behold I-AM living unto the ages) as the APOCALYPTIC PASCHAL-IDENTITY-OATH of the risen-Christ. The egō eimi self-predicate identifies the speaker with the Exodus 3:14 divine-Name; the egenomēn nekros (I-BECAME dead) names the assumed-flesh's-genuine-death — the Word becomes-dead via-the-flesh, the divine-impassibility preserved by-becoming-dead-in-the-flesh-only; the zōn eimi eis tous aiōnas names the resurrection-as-eternal-state. The 'keys of Hades and of Death' name the Word's-Paschal-cosmic-victory-authority. Tewahedo Eastern Easter Trisagion-paschal-chant cites Rev 1:18 as the resurrection-Paschal-acclamation.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, De Incarnatione Verbi (On the Incarnation), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 25 (1857).

entries.summary: 'And the four beasts had each of them six wings about him; and they were full of eyes within: and they rest not day and night, saying, Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty, which was, and is, and is to come' — Athanasius marks the APOCALYPTIC TRISAGION (hagios hagios hagios kyrios ho theos ho pantokratōr) as the ECHO of Isa 6:3's seraphic-trisagion, now-explicitly-Trinitarian in its three-fold-holy. The trisagion is the heavenly-liturgy the earthly-liturgy joins-with (cf. the Sanctus in every Eucharistic-Anaphora). The three-fold-holy is patristically-read as Trinitarian: holy-Father + holy-Son + holy-Spirit, one-Lord-God-Almighty. Athanasius cites the trisagion in Serapion 1.28 against Tropici-pneumatomachian denial of the Spirit's-divinity: the three-fold-holy positively-includes the Spirit in the divine-glory. Tewahedo Anaphora preserves the trisagion as the canonical eucharistic-Trinitarian acclamation.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Epistulae ad Serapionem de Spiritu Sancto (Letters to Serapion on the Holy Spirit, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857). The Serapion correspondence is Athanasius's principal anti-pneumatomachian work, refuting the Tropici denial of the Holy Spirit's divinity and homoousion with Father + Son.

entries.summary: 'And they sung a new song, saying, Thou art worthy to take the book, and to open the seals thereof: for thou wast slain, and hast redeemed us to God by thy blood out of every kindred, and tongue, and people, and nation' — Athanasius marks axios ei labein to biblion... hoti esphagēs kai ēgorasas tō theō en tō haimati sou (thou art WORTHY to take the book... for thou wast slain and hast purchased to God by thy blood) as the APOCALYPTIC REDEMPTION-BY-BLOOD anchor. The worthiness (axios) is HYPER-CREATURELY: only the divine-incarnate could redeem the cosmos. The ēgorasas (purchased / redeemed) is commercial-language: the Word's-blood is the redemption-price. The ek pasēs phylēs kai glōssēs (out of every tribe and tongue) marks the cosmic-scope: the redemption is for all-humanity, not Israel-only. Tewahedo Anaphora cites Rev 5:9 at the Communion-distribution as the universal-redemption-by-blood acclamation.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, De Incarnatione Verbi (On the Incarnation), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 25 (1857).

entries.summary: 'And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God' — Athanasius marks kekletai to onoma autou ho Logos tou theou (his name is-called The Word-of-God) as the APOCALYPTIC LOGOS-CONFIRMATION of the Johannine-prologue. Where Jn 1:1 opens the gospel with en archē ēn ho Logos, kai ho Logos ēn pros ton theon, kai theos ēn ho Logos (in-the-beginning was-the-Word, and the-Word was-with God, and God-was the-Word), Rev 19:13 closes the canonical-Revelation-cycle with the same Word-name-on-the-eschatological-Christ. The vesture-dipped-in-blood (himation bebammenon haimati) carries the Paschal-cross-blood into the eschatological-victory; the Word-of-God-name carries the Johannine-pre-temporal-deity into the eschatological-glory. Tewahedo eschatological-iconography depicts the returning-Christ in vesture-with-Paschal-blood + Logos-name explicitly cited.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth' — Athanasius marks dynamin epelthontos tou Hagiou Pneumatos eph' hymas (power-when-the-Holy-Spirit-has-come-upon you) as the apostolic-succession FORMULA: the same Spirit who-equipped-Christ-as-prophet (Lk 4:18 — Pneuma kyriou ep' eme) now equips the apostolic-Church-as-prophetic-body. The geographical-progression Jerusalem → Judea → Samaria → ends-of-earth is the Spirit's-economic-extension; the Tewahedo Church's foundation through the Ethiopian-eunuch (Acts 8:27-39 → Aksumite tradition) is in the same Spirit-economic-arc.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Epistulae ad Serapionem de Spiritu Sancto (Letters to Serapion on the Holy Spirit, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'Whom God hath raised up, having loosed the pains of death: because it was not possible that he should be holden of it' — Athanasius marks ouk ēn dynaton krateisthai auton hyp' autou (it was-not-possible that he be-held-by it) as the IMPOSSIBILITY-OF-DEATH-HOLDING-THE-WORD. Death cannot hold the deathless-Word; the assumed-flesh died, but the Word's-presence-in-it ensured that death-itself was-defeated-from-within. The Petrine apostolic-kerygma at Pentecost (Acts 2:14-36) is itself an extended argument for the Word's-divinity from the resurrection-FACT-and-its-impossibility-otherwise. Tewahedo Easter Trisagion-Paschal preaching cites Acts 2:24 + Ps 16:10 as the harrowing-Resurrection apostolic-pair.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'This Jesus hath God raised up, whereof we all are witnesses. Therefore being by the right hand of God exalted, and having received of the Father the promise of the Holy Ghost, he hath shed forth this, which ye now see and hear' — Athanasius marks the full PENTECOST-TRINITARIAN-ECONOMY: the Father raises + the Son is exalted-at-the-right-hand + the Son receives-and-pours-out the Spirit. Acts 2:32-33 is the apostolic-kerygmatic articulation of the dual Spirit-economy that Letters to Serapion expounds doctrinally — the Son is BOTH Spirit-recipient (qua-flesh, qua-his-exaltation-as-Man) AND Spirit-sender (qua-divinity, qua-co-source-with-Father). The Pentecost-outpouring IS the incarnational-fulfillment of the Annunciation-overshadowing (Lk 1:35) extended to the Church.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Epistulae ad Serapionem de Spiritu Sancto (Letters to Serapion on the Holy Spirit, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'Therefore let all the house of Israel know assuredly, that God hath made [epoiēsen] that same Jesus, whom ye have crucified, both Lord and Christ' — Athanasius marks epoiēsen (God-MADE) as one of the FOUR HARDEST ARIAN PROOFTEXTS (with Pr 8:22 ektisen-me + Heb 3:2 tō poiēsanti + Acts 2:36). The Arians read epoiēsen as 'made into existence' (= the Son is a creature); Athanasius (CA II.11-18, 8 sections of sustained exegesis) reads as 'appointed-economically' (= the eternal Word was-MADE-Lord-AND-Christ by-his-incarnational-mission, not made-into-existence). The 'made' refers to the ECONOMIC-MISSION (the Word-incarnate's-being-made the Lord-and-Christ of-history-and-humanity), NOT to the Word's-eternal-being. Crucially Pauline-Petrine: Peter's epoiēsen and Paul's gegennēkēn (Heb 1:5 begotten) name complementary aspects — eternal-begetting qua-divinity + economic-making qua-incarnation.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved' — Athanasius marks ouk estin en allō oudeni hē sōtēria (there-is in no other the salvation) as the SOTERIOLOGICAL-EXCLUSIVITY anchor. The name (onoma) is not arbitrary-naming but the divine-Person behind-the-name: only the Word-incarnate can save, because only the Word-by-essence has the divine-power to re-create the fallen image. Petrine apostolic-claim is the same as the Johannine 'no man cometh unto the Father, but by me' (Jn 14:6) — both rest on the Word's-unique-soteriological-capacity-as-divine-incarnate.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, De Incarnatione Verbi (On the Incarnation), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 25 (1857).

entries.summary: 'But he, being full of the Holy Ghost, looked up stedfastly into heaven, and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing on the right hand of God' — Athanasius marks Stephanos plērēs Pneumatos Hagiou (Stephen full of the Holy Spirit) eiden doxan theou kai Iēsoun (saw glory-of-God and Jesus) as the TRINITARIAN-EYE-WITNESS martyrdom-scene: Stephen, IN-the-Spirit, sees the Father-glory + the Son-at-the-right-hand. All three divine Persons are simultaneously-participated-in the witness. The 'standing' (hestōta) — distinct from the usual seated-at-right-hand — is the rare-Acts iconography of Christ-rising-to-receive-the-martyr.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Epistulae ad Serapionem de Spiritu Sancto (Letters to Serapion on the Holy Spirit, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'And he commanded the chariot to stand still: and they went down both into the water, both Philip and the eunuch; and he baptized him' — Athanasius marks the ETHIOPIAN-EUNUCH'S BAPTISM as the DI-§40 canonical-anchor for the Word's-Spirit-empowered missionary-extension to the ends-of-the-earth. The Ethiopian-eunuch is the first-named Gentile-baptismal-recipient in Acts (before Cornelius ch. 10) and the apostolic-tradition that founds Christianity in Aksumite-Tewahedo geography (per Eusebius Hist. Eccl. 2.1.13 + Tewahedo internal tradition). Athanasius — Frumentius's consecrator (c. 330 AD) — was the patriarch who ordained the first Tewahedo bishop, making Acts 8:38 the foundational Athanasian-Tewahedo institutional anchor.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, De Incarnatione Verbi (On the Incarnation), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 25 (1857).

entries.summary: 'And he said, Who art thou, Lord? And the Lord said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest: it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks' — Athanasius marks egō eimi Iēsous hon sy diōkeis (I am Jesus whom thou persecutest) as Christ's IDENTIFICATION-WITH-THE-CHURCH (mystical-body theology). The crucified-and-risen Christ identifies persecution of his disciples as persecution of himself; the Son's-incarnation extends his-Person-and-suffering through the Body. Athanasius pairs Acts 9:5 with Mt 25:40 (insomuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me) as the canonical Christ-mystical-Body identification pair. Tewahedo ecclesiology preserves this mystical-Body-of-Christ reading at the catechetical foundation.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'How God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Ghost and with power: who went about doing good, and healing all that were oppressed of the devil; for God was with him' — Athanasius marks echrisen auton ho theos Pneumati Hagiō (God-anointed him with-Spirit) as the COMMUNICATIO-IDIOMATUM Petrine-anchor. Christ qua-his-assumed-humanity is anointed-by-the-Spirit at the Jordan-baptism (Mt 3:17) and goes about healing-by-the-anointed-Spirit-in-him. Christ qua-his-divinity is the co-source of the Spirit with-the-Father. The same Person anoints and is-anointed; same-Person is Spirit-sender and Spirit-recipient.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'Because he hath appointed a day, in the which he will judge the world in righteousness by that man whom he hath ordained; whereof he hath given assurance unto all men, in that he hath raised him from the dead' — Athanasius marks en andri hō hōrisen (by the man whom he appointed) as the CHRIST-AS-ESCHATOLOGICAL-JUDGE anchor from Paul's Areopagus sermon. The hōrisen (definitely-appointed) + the pistin paraschōn (having-given-assurance) + the anastēsas ek nekrōn (having-raised-from-the-dead) form the apostolic-proof-structure: the resurrection-of-the-Judge is the evidential-guarantee of the eschatological-judgment-to-come. Tewahedo Pantocrator-eschatology cites Acts 17:31 + Mt 25:31-46 as the Judge-Christ apostolic-Gospel pair.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, De Incarnatione Verbi (On the Incarnation), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 25 (1857).

entries.summary: 'Take heed therefore unto yourselves, and to all the flock, over the which the Holy Ghost hath made you overseers, to feed the church of God, which he hath purchased with his own blood' — Athanasius marks tēn ekklēsian tou theou hēn periepoiēsato dia tou haimatos tou idiou (the church of God which he-purchased through his-own blood) as the DIVINE-BLOOD anchor. The 'his own' (tou idiou) and 'God' (theou) co-applied to the blood-purchaser cannot be Arian-accommodated: only one whose-blood-is-God's-own-blood can be the Person Paul names. Pauline-Petrine apostolic-witness to the divine-incarnate's-blood as the Church's purchase-price. Pairs with 1 Pet 1:19 (precious blood of Christ as of a lamb).
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'And he said unto them, Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature' — Athanasius marks poreuthentes eis ton kosmon hapanta kēryxate to euangelion pasē tē ktisei (going into the whole world preach the gospel to every creature) as the MARKAN-Great-Commission, paired with the Mt-28:19-baptismal-formula to form the dual apostolic-mandate. In the canon-defining Festal Letter 39 (367 AD), Athanasius reads the universal-Gospel-mandate as the basis for the NT-canon's twenty-seven-book delimitation — the gospel-preached-to-every-creature requires a definite-corpus-of-apostolic-writings to be-preached-from. The Tewahedo NT-canon (broader than the Athanasian 27 — including 1 Clement, Shepherd of Hermas, etc.) is in continuous reception with the Athanasian Festal-39 paradigm.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Festal Letters (selections, including the canon-defining Letter 39 of 367 AD), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD.

entries.summary: 'He saith unto them, How then doth David in spirit call him Lord, saying, The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand, till I make thine enemies thy footstool?' — Athanasius marks David en Pneumati kalei auton kyrion (David in-the-Spirit calls him Lord) as the SCRIPTURE-PNEUMATIC-INSPIRATION + DAVIDIC-SON-IS-DAVIDIC-LORD double-anchor. The Spirit-of-prophecy gave David the Ps 110:1-vision of his-Son-as-his-Lord — the Davidic-Son's-pre-Davidic-divinity. Christ's own argument in Mt 22:41-46 is Athanasius's exegetical-paradigm for reading the Old Testament: every OT-pre-Christian text was-spoken-in-the-Spirit and pointed-Christologically toward the Word's incarnation.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away' — Athanasius marks hoi de logoi mou ou mē parelthōsin (my words shall by-no-means pass-away) as Christ's-self-predication of DIVINE-WORD-ETERNITY. Cosmic-perishability is contrasted with the words-of-Christ-perishability: cosmos can-pass-away (entropic-finitude); Christ's words-cannot. Only divine-words-can-claim-eternity-of-non-perishing — Athanasius reads as direct-self-divine-claim (paired with Mt 5:18 jot-and-tittle-shall-not-pass). The Tewahedo Liturgy preserves this eternal-Word claim at the Gospel-procession: Christ's words are the imperishable-substance of the lectionary.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'When the Son of man shall come in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory' — Athanasius marks ho Huios tou anthrōpou en tē doxē autou (the Son-of-Man in HIS glory) as the eschatological-RETURN-IN-GLORY Christology. The glory is autou (his-own); the angels accompany (met' autou pantes hoi angeloi); the throne is tou doxēs autou (of-his-glory). All three predicates are divine: only YHWH has-his-own-glory, is-attended-by-all-angels, and sits-on-the-throne-of-glory. Mt 25:31 is the eschatological-counterpart to Acts 17:31 (Christ as appointed-Judge). Tewahedo iconography of the Pantocrator-on-the-throne is iconographically-anchored at Mt 25:31.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, De Incarnatione Verbi (On the Incarnation), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 25 (1857).

entries.summary: 'Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am' — Athanasius marks prin Abraam genesthai egō eimi (before Abraham came-to-be, I AM) as Christ's DIRECT ARTICULATION OF THE DIVINE NAME (Exo 3:14 egō eimi ho ōn). The tense-juxtaposition is crucial: Abraham came-to-be (genesthai, aorist-of-becoming, creaturely-temporality) versus I AM (eimi, present-of-eternal-being, divine-timelessness). The Word's pre-Abrahamic-existence is not 'older-than-Abraham' (which would be creaturely-comparative) but in-a-different-tense entirely — eternal-being-versus-temporal-becoming. The Jewish-interlocutors recognize the blasphemy-claim and pick up stones to kill him (Jn 8:59), confirming they-understood the egō-eimi as divine-self-identification.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth: for he shall not speak of himself; but whatsoever he shall hear, that shall he speak: and he will shew you things to come' — Athanasius marks the SPIRIT-OF-TRUTH ECONOMIC-MISSION as the Trinitarian-economy-of-revelation: the Spirit is sent-by-the-Son (who-is-the-truth, Jn 14:6), receives-from-the-Son (everything he speaks is from-the-Son), and guides-believers-into-the-Son. The Spirit's-procession-and-mission is Christo-centric in its economic-form. Jn 16:13 is the principal Johannine anchor for the doctrine that Letters to Serapion expounds: the Spirit, though distinct-Person from Father and Son, is homoousios with both and stands in unbroken-economic-coordination.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Epistulae ad Serapionem de Spiritu Sancto (Letters to Serapion on the Holy Spirit, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'And when all things shall be subdued unto him, then shall the Son also himself be subject unto him that put all things under him, that God may be all in all' — Athanasius marks hina ē ho theos panta en pasin (that God may-be all in all) as the ESCHATOLOGICAL-TRINITARIAN-RESTORATION anchor. The subjection (hypotagēsetai) of the Son to the Father is NOT subordinationist — it is the Son's-redemptive-mission-completed handing-back the redeemed-cosmos to the Father; the Son's-economy-of-subjection is qua-his-assumed-humanity-and-mission, not qua-his-divinity. The 'God all in all' is the Trinitarian-Father-Son-Spirit perichoretic-restoration of all things in their proper relation to the divine-Source.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'One Lord, one faith, one baptism, One God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in you all' — Athanasius marks the SEVENFOLD-HENOTĒS (heis Kyrios + mia pistis + hen baptisma + heis theos kai Patēr pantōn) as the TRINITARIAN-MONOTHEISM Pauline-synthesis. The seven 'ones' do not flatten the Trinitarian-distinctions but articulate the divine-unity-in-Trinity: one-Lord (the Son), one-baptism (in the Trinity per Mt 28:19), one-Spirit (implied; cf. Eph 4:4 above), one-God-and-Father — the Three are the unique-one-God. The eph' hēmin pantōn (above all, through all, in you all) names the Father's universal-divine-presence operating through the Son and in the Spirit.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Epistulae ad Serapionem de Spiritu Sancto (Letters to Serapion on the Holy Spirit, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'When Christ, who is our life, shall appear, then shall ye also appear with him in glory' — Athanasius marks ho Christos hē zōē hymōn (Christ, the life of-yours) as the THEŌSIS-ESCHATOLOGICAL-SUMMIT anchor: Christ IS the believer's-life-itself (not merely-the-source-of-life). When-he-appears (phanerōthē — eschatological-manifestation), believers-appear-with-him-in-glory — the theōsis-grant fulfilled at the eschaton. Athanasius's signature formula 'He was made man that we might be made God' (DI §54) reaches its temporal-completion at the Col 3:4 phanerōsis. The Tewahedo Easter-vigil hymnody cites Col 3:4 as the saint-glorified-with-Christ Paschal-fulfillment.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, De Incarnatione Verbi (On the Incarnation), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 25 (1857).

entries.summary: 'Now the God of peace, that brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant' — Athanasius marks ho theos tēs eirēnēs ho anagagōn ek nekrōn ton kyrion (the God of peace who brought up from-the-dead the Lord) as the TRINITARIAN-RESURRECTION pastoral-doxology. The Father-of-peace brings up the Son through-the-blood-of-the-eternal-covenant (haimati diathēkēs aiōniou — note aiōniou, eternal, pointing to the Trinitarian-counsel before-time). The doxological-frame is what makes Hebrews's-Christology WORSHIP-able: every Christological-claim climaxes in doxology to the Father through the Son.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning' — Athanasius marks ho Patēr tōn phōtōn par' hō ouk eni parallagē ē tropēs aposkiasma (the Father of lights, with-whom is-not variation or shadow-of-turning) as the DIVINE-IMMUTABILITY anchor. The atrepton (un-turning) and aparal-lakton (un-varying) of the Father's-essence are direct anti-Arian: the divine-Light cannot vary or turn (i.e. cannot become what-it-was-not, cannot beget-a-creature-rather-than-eternal-Word). Athanasius's inclusion of James in the NT-canon (Festal Letter 39, 367 AD) was the canonical-decision that gave the Catholic-Epistle its full-apostolic-authority in the Eastern tradition; Jas 1:17 anchors the canon-inclusion with a direct-Trinitarian-essence prooftext.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Festal Letters (selections, including the canon-defining Letter 39 of 367 AD), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD.

entries.summary: 'And we know that the Son of God is come, and hath given us an understanding, that we may know him that is true, and we are in him that is true, even in his Son Jesus Christ. This is the true God, and eternal life' — Athanasius marks houtos estin ho alēthinos theos kai zōē aiōnios (THIS is the true God and eternal life) as the MOST EXPLICIT EXPLICIT-DEITY-OF-THE-SON Johannine-Catholic-Epistle anchor. The houtos (THIS — referring back to Jesus Christ in the immediately-preceding phrase) directly-names Christ as ho alēthinos theos (THE TRUE God, with definite article + qualifying-adjective). The Arians could not Arian-accommodate this without breaking standard Greek; Athanasius cites it as definitive against any creature-Christology.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance' — Athanasius marks mē boulomenos tinas apolesthai alla pantas eis metanoian chōrēsai (not willing any to perish but all to come to-repentance) as the DIVINE-UNIVERSAL-SALVIFIC-WILL Petrine-anchor. The divine-patience (makrothymia) is itself-incarnational: the Word's-incarnation IS the divine-patience-extended-in-time, giving humanity-time to repent. Athanasius's DI §6-7 anti-Manichaean reading of evil-as-privation-of-good rests on this universal-salvific-will: God-cannot-be-the-author-of-evil because his-will-is-toward-universal-restoration.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, De Incarnatione Verbi (On the Incarnation), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 25 (1857).

entries.summary: 'The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want' (LXX 22:1 — kyrios poimainei me kai ouden me hysterēsei) — Athanasius marks Ps 23 (LXX 22) as the PARADIGMATIC PASTORAL-COMFORT-PSALM in the Letter to Marcellinus: prescribed for the soul-tending-toward-providential-trust. The kyrios poimainei me (the Lord shepherds-me) is read Christologically — the Word-incarnate is the Johannine ho poimēn ho kalos (the Good Shepherd, Jn 10:11). The Athanasian pastoral-spiritual hermeneutic transforms the Psalter into a Christic-prayer-book: each Psalm voices a stance-toward-Christ that the praying-soul takes-up. The Tewahedo Säʿatat (Liturgy of the Hours) Psalter-pattern preserves this Athanasian pastoral-Psalter use.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Epistola ad Marcellinum de Interpretatione Psalmorum (Letter to Marcellinus on the Interpretation of the Psalms), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 27 (1857). The Letter is Athanasius's principal pastoral-spiritual work — a personal letter to Marcellinus (recovering from illness) explaining how to use each Psalm as prayer for specific spiritual circumstances. Hermeneutic anchor for the Tewahedo Office (Säʿatat) Psalter-recitation tradition.

entries.summary: 'Have mercy upon me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness: according unto the multitude of thy tender mercies blot out my transgressions' (LXX 50:3) — Athanasius marks Ps 51 (LXX 50) as the PENITENTIAL-PRAYER PARADIGM in the Letter to Marcellinus: prescribed for the soul-confessing-grave-sin. The eleēson me ho theos kata to mega eleos sou (have mercy on me, O God, according-to thy great-mercy) becomes the canonical-confession-formula for the Tewahedo penitential-tradition. Athanasius's pastoral-instruction: pray Ps 51 not as one observing-David-confessing (third-person) but as one's-OWN-confession-in-David's-voice. The Psalter is the Spirit-given prayer-vocabulary the praying-soul inhabits.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Epistola ad Marcellinum de Interpretatione Psalmorum (Letter to Marcellinus on the Interpretation of the Psalms), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 27 (1857). The Letter is Athanasius's principal pastoral-spiritual work — a personal letter to Marcellinus (recovering from illness) explaining how to use each Psalm as prayer for specific spiritual circumstances. Hermeneutic anchor for the Tewahedo Office (Säʿatat) Psalter-recitation tradition.

entries.summary: 'Cast me not away from thy presence; and take not thy holy spirit from me' (LXX 50:13 — to Pneuma to Hagion sou mē antanelēs ap' emou) — Athanasius marks Ps 51:11 (LXX 50:13) as the OT ANTI-PNEUMATOMACHIAN ANCHOR — cited in Letters to Serapion 1.9 against Tropici denial of the Spirit's divinity. The Pneuma to Hagion sou (thy-Holy-Spirit, with possessive-divine-pronoun) makes the Spirit the inalienable-divine-property of God; one does-not-pray-to-not-remove a creature from oneself but God's-own-Spirit. David's-prayer thus articulates pneumatological-divinity centuries before the post-Nicene Trinitarian-articulation. Pairs with Ps 139:7 + 143:10 as the canonical-OT-Holy-Spirit prooftext-triplet.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Epistulae ad Serapionem de Spiritu Sancto (Letters to Serapion on the Holy Spirit, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

entries.summary: 'O LORD God of my salvation, I have cried day and night before thee' (LXX 87:2) — Athanasius marks Ps 88 (LXX 87) as the AFFLICTION-PRAYER PARADIGM in the Letter to Marcellinus: prescribed for the soul-in-affliction-without-relief. Ps 88 is the darkest of the canonical Psalms (ending on darkness, not deliverance — phrasē mou aphēste philos kai plēsion kai tous gnōstous mou apo talaipōrias, 'thou hast put far from me lover and friend, and my acquaintances into darkness'). Athanasius's pastoral-counsel: the Psalter does not prescribe Ps 88 lightly; but for the soul-in-severe-affliction, even the dark-Psalm is Spirit-given consolation — the very-act-of-voicing-affliction-to-God IS the saving-prayer.
entries.attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Epistola ad Marcellinum de Interpretatione Psalmorum (Letter to Marcellinus on the Interpretation of the Psalms), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 27 (1857). The Letter is Athanasius's principal pastoral-spiritual work — a personal letter to Marcellinus (recovering from illness) explaining how to use each Psalm as prayer for specific spiritual circumstances. Hermeneutic anchor for the Tewahedo Office (Säʿatat) Psalter-recitation tradition.

entries.summary: 'He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty' (LXX 90:1 — ho katoikōn en boētheia tou Hypsistou en skepē tou theou tou ouranou aulisthēsetai) — Athanasius marks Ps 91 (LXX 90) as the DIVINE-PROTECTION PARADIGM in the Letter to Marcellinus: prescribed for the soul-seeking-refuge-from-physical-and-spiritual-dangers. The shadow-of-the-Most-High (skepē tou Hypsistou) is read Christ-ologically — the Word-incarnate is the divine-shadow-cast-on-earth, the Annunciation-overshadowing (Lk 1:35 episkiasei soi) now-extended to every believer. The Tewahedo travel-blessing tradition cites Ps 91 as the Mäzmurä Dawit (David's Psalter) protective-prayer.

entries.summary: 'Thy word have I hid in mine heart, that I might not sin against thee' (LXX 118:11 — en tē kardia mou ekrypsa ta logia sou hopōs an mē hamartō soi) — Athanasius marks Ps 119 (LXX 118) — the longest-Psalm, structured by the Hebrew-alphabet — as the WORD-INTERNALIZATION PARADIGM in the Letter to Marcellinus. The praying-soul does not merely-recite-the-word but HIDES-IT-IN-THE-HEART (ekrypsa en tē kardia) as protective-talisman-against-sin. The logia (oracles/divine-utterances) are Spirit-breathed-Scripture, and their-hiding-in-the-heart is the Spirit's-work-of-sanctifying-memory. Athanasius's pastoral-instruction: memorize the Psalter completely; the soul that knows-the-Psalter-by-heart has the Spirit's-prayer-vocabulary always-at-hand.

entries.work: First Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan I)
entries.summary: 'We have the God of our fathers, to whom we bow down — He who created heaven and earth, the sea and what is in it, the sun and the moon, the stars and the clouds. He is the true God whom we worship and in whom we trust' — the Meqabyan brothers' creation-confession of faith, framed as a CREEDAL CORRECTIVE that inverts the Chaldean king Ṣiruṣaydan's claim at 1:26-27 that his idols created the heavens, sun, moon, stars, winds and rains. The creation-formula correctly reassigns creation to the God of the patriarchs. Functions liturgically as the EOTC anti-idolatry creed rooted in the first commandment + Genesis 1 creation-account.

entries.work: First Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan I)
entries.summary: 'Unless you bring us those warriors — THE MEQABYANS — we will burn your city with fire' — THE EPONYM VERSE of the entire trilogy. The king's troops apply the collective designation መቃብያንን (the Meqabyans) to Maqabis-of-Benjamin's sons. From this naming the ENTIRE THREE-BOOK TRILOGY (1 Mq + 2 Mq + 3 Mq) takes its title. The Geʽez form, retained in the Amharic, is the source of all later renderings (Meqabyan, Maqabyan, Maccabean in popular English usage). Per Horovitz 1905 p. 195 fn. 3 + Dillmann Lexicon Linguae Aethiopicae (1865): etymology shows Seleucid-coin attestation under Antiochus IV — but the Ethiopian Meqabyan narrative is otherwise INDEPENDENT of the Greek Maccabees (Horovitz 'von Christus nirgends die Rede'; the books are distinctively Ethiopian in content).

entries.work: First Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan I)
entries.summary: 'They turned their faces toward the east, and stretching out their hands, they prayed together to God' — the eastward orientation in prayer is a FIXED EOTC LITURGICAL POSTURE (codified in Didascalia Apostolorum II.57, retained in Ethiopian practice). The verse's opening prayer-question functions as the brothers seeking divine-permission to refuse the king's edict — the resistance is not spontaneous defiance but a SANCTIONED ACT sought through prayer. Parallels Daniel 6:10 (Daniel praying with windows opened toward Jerusalem). The Tewahedo Office (Säʿatat / Liturgy of the Hours) preserves eastward-prayer as the canonical posture for all liturgical prayer.
