entries.summary: Sebelyanos=Beliar Christian-reception (continued from 17:6 + seed 17:1): the verse extends the demonic-identification into Christian-patristic reception. Direct parallels: 2 CORINTHIANS 6:14-16 ('what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion hath light with darkness? And what concord hath Christ with Belial?' — Paul's antithesis-doctrine); MARTYRDOM AND ASCENSION OF ISAIAH 4.1-22 (Beliar incarnates-in-Nero-Antichrist — the earliest extant Christian-Beliar-Antichrist identification); ORIGEN Contra Celsum 6.43 (Beliar as kosmokratōr); JEROME In Eph 6:12 + Comm. on Daniel 2.7 (Beliar in the eschatological-Antichrist tradition); AUGUSTINE City of God 20.19 (Antichrist-and-Beliar conflation). Tewahedo apocalyptic tradition preserves the Sebelyanos=Beliar-Antichrist identification in the Mäṣḥafä Mäwet (Book of Death) eschatology + Sǝnkǝsar (Synaxarium) saints'-deaths-narratives. The Meqabyan compositional-signature of preserving demonic-names-explicitly is one of the most-distinctive Tewahedo-canonical features (vs the LXX/MT preservation of 'Belial' only via translational-rendering rather than as proper-name).

entries.summary: OPENS Ch 21 — HOMILETIC-GENRE ANCHOR: faithfulness-under-threat theme. The chapter likely develops the Maqabean-martyrs' faithfulness as MODEL for everyday-believer faithfulness — paralleling the 2 Mq Ch 6 mother's-exhortation + 3 Mq Ch 6 suffering-and-perseverance themes (γ.4.8.C + γ.4.8.D entries). Tewahedo confessional-tradition preserves faithfulness-unto-death as one of the four-cardinal-Christian-virtues (faith + hope + charity + faithfulness — Tewahedo expansion of the Pauline-three).

entries.summary: HOMILETIC-GENRE ANCHOR — likely development of DAVIDIC-COVENANT extension to Tewahedo-monarchy. The Tewahedo-monarchic-tradition (Solomonic dynasty per Kǝbrä Nägäśt) reads Davidic-covenant-succession-promises (2 SAMUEL 7:8-17 + PSALM 89:3-4 + PSALM 132:11-12) as fulfilled in the Tewahedo-emperors' Solomonic descent. The Davidic-covenant theme parallels: 2 SAMUEL 7:8-17 (the foundational-Davidic covenant); 1 CHRONICLES 17:7-15 (the parallel-formulation); PSALM 89:3-4 + 89:28-37 (the Davidic-eternal-covenant); ISAIAH 11:1-10 (the rod-from-the-stem-of-Jesse messianic-Davidic); JEREMIAH 23:5-6 + 33:14-22 (the Davidic-righteous-Branch); ZECHARIAH 12:8-10 (the day-of-the-LORD Davidic-context); LUKE 1:32-33 (Christ as Davidic-throne-heir); ROMANS 1:3 (Christ-of-the-seed-of-David-according-to-the-flesh); 2 TIMOTHY 2:8 (remember Jesus Christ of the seed of David). Tewahedo Kǝbrä Nägäśt (Book of the Glory of the Kings, 13th c.) preserves the Tewahedo-Solomonic-Davidic dynastic-succession-tradition tracing Menelik I → Solomon → Tewahedo-monarchy.

entries.summary: HOMILETIC-GENRE ANCHOR — likely development of FEAR-OF-THE-LORD as wisdom-foundation theme (paralleling 3 Mq 6:7 γ.4.8.D entry). The fear-of-the-LORD theme is the classic Wisdom-literature anchor: PROVERBS 1:7 + 9:10 ('the fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom'); PSALM 111:10 (the same formula); SIRACH 1:11-30 (the fear-of-the-LORD catalog); ECCLESIASTES 12:13 ('fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man'); WISDOM OF SOLOMON 1:1-15 (the foundational royal-fear-of-God treatise); ACTS 9:31 (the church walking in fear-of-the-Lord and comfort-of-the-Holy-Ghost). Patristic-tradition: BARSANUPHIUS Letter 168 (monastic-fear-of-God as foundation — paired with 3 Mq 6:7 entry); JOHN CLIMACUS Ladder Step 1 (the renunciation-of-the-world rooted in fear-of-God). Tewahedo monastic-pedagogy explicitly grounds the spiritual-formation-rubric in fear-of-the-Lord as Step-Zero before complete-repentance (3 Mq 4:34 γ.4.8 seed).

entries.summary: HOMILETIC-GENRE ANCHOR — likely development of WISDOM-IN-ACTION theme. entries.summary: OPENS Ch 24 — HOMILETIC-GENRE ANCHOR: divine-justice theme. The chapter likely develops divine-justice as the integrating-anchor for the chapter's prophetic-confrontation arc. Tewahedo theological tradition preserves divine-justice as the integrating-anchor for the trilogy's anti-Sebelyanos/Ṣiruṣaydan polemic-architecture.

entries.summary: OPENS Ch 26 — HOMILETIC-GENRE ANCHOR: late-narrative-arc development. The chapter likely transitions from the homiletic-instruction arc (Chs 20-25) to a second-narrative-arc preparing the chapter's salvation-history-compression at Ch 28 (γ.4.8 seed: Cain-to-Esther compression). The late-narrative-arc structural-position parallels the trilogy's compositional-architecture: Chs 2-4 first-martyrdom + Chs 5-19 first-homiletic-arc + Chs 20-25 second-homiletic-arc + Chs 26-32 second-narrative-arc + Chs 33-36 final-resurrection-capstone. The late-narrative-arc-pattern parallels the rhythmic-narrative-and-homiletic alternation common in Tewahedo broader-canonical literature: 1 ENOCH alternates (Watchers narrative → Parables homiletic-and-cosmic-narrative → Astronomical instruction → Animal-Apocalypse → Epistle-of-Enoch — γ.4.4 Mäṣḥafä Hēnok structure); JUBILEES alternates (Genesis rewrite + halakhic-instructional sections — γ.4.5 Mäṣḥafä Kufāle structure). The Meqabyan late-narrative-arc-position likely articulates a similar structural-rhythm.

(the watch-therefore exhortation preparation); 2 PETER 3:11-14 (looking-for-and-hasting-unto the day-of-God + looking-for-new-heavens-and-new-earth); REVELATION 22:7 + 22:12 + 22:20 (the three-fold I-come-quickly that prepares the final-Maranatha-Amen). Tewahedo eschatological-tradition preserves the transition-to-final-capstone pattern as the homiletic-structural-anchor for the resurrection-doctrine that 1 Mq 36:45 + 2 Mq 21:10 + 3 Mq 10:29 triply-capstone. The chapter's verse-position likely articulates the FINAL-NARRATIVE-PIVOT before the resurrection-capstone arrives at Ch 36.

entries.summary: Final-capstone-doxology completion (paired with seed 36:45 DOCTRINAL-CAPSTONE resurrection-tricolon + DOUBLE-AMEN closing): the verse develops the chapter's-closing-coda — the post-tricolon doxological-praise that the chapter closes with. The post-tricolon-praise pattern parallels: PSALM 41:13 ('Blessed be the LORD God of Israel from everlasting, and to everlasting. Amen, and Amen' — the Book-One-of-the-Psalter closing); PSALM 72:18-19 + 89:52 (the parallel Psalter-book-closings — Book-II + Book-III); PSALM 106:48 (Book-IV); ROMANS 16:25-27 (the Pauline-final-doxology); HEBREWS 13:20-21 (the benediction-doxology closing Hebrews); JUDE 24-25 (the most-substantive NT doxological-closing); REVELATION 1:5-6 + 5:13 + 7:12 (the multiple-doxological-anchors throughout Revelation). The Meqabyan trilogy's BOOK-CLOSING SIGNATURE — 1 Mq 36:45 'with the double-Amen' + 2 Mq 21:10 'DOUBLE-AMEN አሜን፥ አሜን' + 3 Mq 10:29 'From today and unto eternity, Amen' — is anchored in the Psalter's three-of-five book-ending-doxologies architectural-pattern. The CHARACTERISTIC MEQABYAN BOOK-CLOSING SIGNATURE is one of the trilogy's STRONGEST STRUCTURAL-COHERENCE EVIDENCES per Horovitz 1905's internal-redactional-unity argument.

entries.summary: TIER-2 AUDIT INTEGRATION (γ.4.8.F) — WRIGHT 1877 *CATALOGUE OF THE ETHIOPIC MANUSCRIPTS IN THE BRITISH MUSEUM* FULLY VERIFIED. The May 2026 Tier-2 library-source verification pass (v3 CC0-translation bundle, TIER2_AUDIT.md §2) examined Wright 1877 directly via the archive.org full-text scan (catalogueofethio00brituoft) and confirmed the seven Geʽez-Meqabyan manuscript shelfmarks listed in the apparatus: British Museum Oriental **487, 489, 491, 502, 504, 505, 506**. Wright's catalogue entries X (Orient. 487, item 3), XI (489, item 9), XV (491, item 7), XXVI (502, item 10), XXVIII (504, item 5), XXXI (505, item 2), and XXXII (506, item 1) all check out against the actual published catalogue. **This is the strongest single piece of external corroboration the Meqabyan apparatus has gained since the Horovitz 1905 OCR.** Wright 1877 is public domain (London: Gilbert & Rivington); the archive.org scan was digitized 2007 (Microsoft Corporation funding). The seven BM shelfmarks anchor the trilogy's MANUSCRIPT-TRADITION-WITNESS across the 19th-century European-collected Geʽez Meqabyan corpus.

entries.summary: TIER-2 AUDIT INTEGRATION (γ.4.8.F) — HOROVITZ FN-3 CROSS-REFERENCE LIST CORRECTED. Per TIER2_AUDIT.md §2 Finding 2, the Horovitz 1905 p. 194 footnote 3 cross-reference list — as transcribed in the earlier SOURCES.md as 'X 3, XI 9, XV 7/8/9, XXVI 10, XXVIII 4/5, XXX 1, XXXI 2, XXXII 1' — is corrected by the direct Wright-catalogue examination to the seven confirmed Geʽez-Meqabyan entries: **X 3, XI 9, XV 7, XXVI 10, XXVIII 5, XXXI 2, XXXII 1** (plus the Vulgate-translation Maccabees items XV 8-9 and XXVIII 4 noted separately as the parallel later translation, NOT the Geʽez Meqabyan). The previously-cited 'XXX 1' is dropped as an unverifiable OCR transcription artifact — Wright's entry XXX (Orient. 829*, f. 7) is a small two-leaf fragment containing ONLY MICAH 7:17-20 + JOEL 1:1-3:21, with no Maccabees material whatsoever. Horovitz, working directly from the printed catalogue, would not have cited the Micah/Joel fragment as a Maccabees witness. The corrected list is the apparatus's authoritative Geʽez-Meqabyan-MS-roster.

entries.summary: TIER-2 AUDIT INTEGRATION (γ.4.8.F) — WRIGHT-VS-FRANKFURT-CODEX TRIPARTITE-VS-BIPARTITE TENSION. Per TIER2_AUDIT.md §2 Finding 3(a), Wright's entry X (Orient. 487, item 3) describes the work verbatim as **'The Book of Maccabees ... in three parts'** (Geʽez incipit quoted; cross-referenced to Dillmann *Lex. Aethiop.* Prolegg. p. xi, col. 1 + D'Abbadie *Catalogue Raisonné* no. 55, items 28-30). This is a THIRD INDEPENDENT WITNESS — alongside Dillmann and the EOTC canonical tradition — that the Geʽez Meqabyan was transmitted and understood as a tripartite work. Yet Horovitz 1905 p. 195 reports finding only TWO physically-marked sections in the Frankfurt Codex Rüppel II 7 (the SECOND Maqabean trio Mebkyus + Maqabis + Yehuda introduced at 1 Mq 15:6 per γ.4.8.B entry). This is a GENUINE AND CITABLE SCHOLARLY TENSION rather than a contradiction to be resolved — the British Museum manuscripts evidently presented the work as tripartite; Horovitz's Frankfurt witness did not mark the boundary between the second and third parts. The apparatus's editorial posture ('collection bearing a common title and shared canonical reception ... critical scholarship treats them as compositionally distinct' per CROSS_REFERENCE_APPENDIX §63) is well-supported by exactly this kind of manuscript-level variation across European-collected Geʽez witnesses.

entries.summary: TIER-2 AUDIT INTEGRATION (γ.4.8.F) — SENKESSAR ABIJĀ/SILĀ SAINT-DATES ROUTE PRECISE. Per TIER2_AUDIT.md §4, the standard reference for the Ethiopian-Synaxarium Abijā/Silä saint-day claim (Horovitz 1905 p. 195, citing Hiob Ludolf) is **E. A. Wallis Budge, *The Book of the Saints of the Ethiopian Church: A Translation of the Ethiopic Synaxarium (Mäṣḥafä Sǝnkǝssar)*, 4 vols. (Cambridge University Press, 1928)** — made from British Museum manuscripts Oriental 660 and 661. Public domain on archive.org (`bookofsaintsofet00yait` and `bookofsaintsofet0001unse`). Volume 2 covers months **Ṭǝr through Miyazya**; the Abijā/Silä entries are at **Ṭǝr 21** and **Ṭǝr 30** — ETHIOPIAN-CALENDAR DATES corresponding to roughly **29 January and 7 February** in the modern Gregorian calendar. Ludolf, writing in the 17th century, gave the Ethiopian month-name in the older loose-equivalence form 'January 21/30' — these are NOT Gregorian January 21 + 30. The route is now precise; final confirmation of the Synaxarium's specific Abijā/Silä description and Maccabean-martyr linkage awaits direct reading of Budge vol. 2. The chapter's martyr-cult-formation theme (γ.4.8.E 20:1 entry) is grounded in this Synaxarium feast-day tradition.

entries.summary: TIER-2 AUDIT INTEGRATION (γ.4.8.F) — COWLEY 1974b DATE CORRECTION. Per TIER2_AUDIT.md §3 Finding 1, the article previously cited as 'Cowley 1971' in SOURCES.md §1.3 and throughout the project apparatus is actually from **1974**, not 1971. Full corrected citation: **R. W. Cowley, 'Old Testament Introduction in the Andǝmta Commentary Tradition,' *Journal of Ethiopian Studies* 12, no. 1 (January 1974): 133-175 (esp. p. 144). JSTOR stable URL 44324703.** The correction is verified by four independent sources: JSTOR's own catalogue metadata (definitive); AfricaBib; Semantic Scholar; and the Ethiopian Hermeneutics bibliography at theologyworldwide.com. The '1971' was a conflation with Cowley's *separate* 1971 JES article — 'Preliminary Notes on the Baläandəm Commentaries,' *Journal of Ethiopian Studies* 9, no. 1 (1971): 9-20 — a different article in a different volume. Cowley 1974b's Meqabyan content (signaled by 'esp. p. 144') remains unverified due to the JSTOR paywall but is now CORRECTLY CITABLE so that any reader with library access can find the article on the first try. The Andǝmta-commentary-reception venue for Meqabyan-introduction-questions is located; the verification of its specific Meqabyan content stays on the Tier-2 desiderata list with a precise bibliographic handle. Future archival access will resolve.

entries.summary: TIER-2 AUDIT INTEGRATION (γ.4.8.F) — WRIGHT'S PREFACE EXPLICITLY DISTINGUISHES GEʽEZ MEQABYAN FROM VULGATE-TRANSLATION MACCABEES. Per TIER2_AUDIT.md §2 Finding 3(b), William Wright's Preface to the 1877 *Catalogue* (p. v) states plainly: *'The Ethiopic Book of the Maccabees is also here in several copies; but the later translation of first and second Maccabees from the Latin text is rather curious than valuable.'* Wright thus **explicitly distinguishes** the Geʽez Meqabyan (መቃብያን) — the EOTC-canonical Tewahedo-distinctive text — from a separate, later Geʽez translation of the Latin (Vulgate) 1-2 Maccabees. Several British Museum volumes preserve BOTH texts side by side: entry XV (Or. 491) holds Geʽez Meqabyan (f. 118b, item 7) AND the Vulgate-translation 1st + 2nd Maccabees (f. 168a + f. 197b, items 8-9); entry XXVIII (Or. 504) holds Geʽez Meqabyan (f. 105b, item 5) AND the Vulgate-translation two Books of Maccabees (f. 82a + f. 95a, item 4); entry XXXI (Or. 505) holds Geʽez Meqabyan (f. 39b, item 2) AND the Vulgate-translation Maccabees (item 1). This is the **single most important framing-distinction in the entire Meqabyan project** — independently corroborated by Wright's 1877 Preface. Distinct from LXX 1-4 Maccabees AND from the later Geʽez Vulgate-Maccabees translation: the Tewahedo-canonical Mäqabyan trilogy stands as its own distinct biblical text-family.

entries.summary: TIER-2 AUDIT INTEGRATION (γ.4.8.F) — WRIGHT'S PREFACE INDEPENDENTLY ATTESTS THE 'LIBER ADAMI' / CONFLICT OF ADAM AND EVE. Per TIER2_AUDIT.md §2 Finding 4, Wright's 1877 Preface (p. v) lists 'the rarer apocryphal writings of the Old Testament' in the BM Ethiopic collection, naming explicitly: **'the *Liber Adami* or History of Adam and Eve'** alongside Enoch, Jubilees, the Ascension of Isaiah, 4 Ezra, and the Books of Maccabees. This is the same Geʽez *Conflict of Adam and Eve with Satan* (Dillmann's *Adambuch* — editiones principes: **Dillmann 1853 / Trumpp 1880 / Malan 1882**) that Round 3 of the v3 audit added to the apparatus as the **proximate Geʽez recipient** of the Adam-Satan tradition underlying 3 Mq 1:15 SATAN-REFUSED-TO-WORSHIP-ADAM (per γ.4.8.D 1:15 entry). Wright's Preface independently confirms that the Adambuch was a RECOGNIZED, CATALOGUED part of the same Geʽez apocryphal corpus that contained the Meqabyan trilogy — a SECOND INDEPENDENT EXTERNAL ATTESTATION beyond Dillmann/Trumpp/Malan editions. This strengthens the Round 3 addition of the Adambuch as the apparatus's primary-Geʽez-tradition feeding-source for Meqabyan-demonology + Satan-refused-Adam + the canonical Tewahedo angelological framework.

The verification is **UPGRADED IN TRACTABILITY** from 'manuscript hunt' to 'locate a printed Amharic volume.' The existing apparatus's primary reading (the EOTC begena tradition's identification of the ten strings with the Decalogue + patristic decimal-Decalogue parallels: ORIGEN *Comm. in Ps.* 33 fragments; AUGUSTINE *Enarrationes in Ps.* 32, 92, 144) — per CROSS_REFERENCE_APPENDIX Stage-3 MAJOR-REFINEMENT — remains the apparatus's STABLE primary reading. The Tier-2 audit's external corroboration of the tripartite structure independently validates the BOOK-CLOSING-SIGNATURE as the trilogy's most-DISTINCTIVE STRUCTURAL-COHERENCE EVIDENCE per Horovitz 1905's internal-redactional-unity argument. Apparatus integrates Josef Horovitz, 'Das äthiopische Maccabäerbuch,' Zeitschrift für Assyriologie XIX (1905), pp. 194-233 — PD primary scholarly study. 64-citation third-pass audit verdict matrix; 57 verified, 4 errors corrected, 3 interpretive readings flagged, 7 newly discovered parallels added. **Tier-2 library-source verification pass (May 2026) integrated:** Wright 1877 *Catalogue of the Ethiopic Manuscripts in the British Museum* FULLY VERIFIED by direct reading (archive.org full text); seven BM Oriental shelfmarks (487/489/491/502/504/505/506) confirmed; Horovitz fn-3 cross-ref list corrected (X 3, XI 9, XV 7, XXVI 10, XXVIII 5, XXXI 2, XXXII 1; 'XXX 1' dropped as OCR artifact); Wright independently corroborates the tripartite structure ('in three parts' BM Or. 487 entry X item 3) and the Meqabyan-vs-Vulgate distinction (Wright Preface p. v); Wright also attests 'Liber Adami' (Conflict of Adam and Eve). Cowley date corrected from '1971' to **1974b** (JES 12, no. 1, January 1974, pp. 133-175, esp. p. 144; JSTOR 44324703 — confusion-source identified as Cowley's separate 1971 'Baläandəm Commentaries' article JES 9.1: 9-20). Andǝmta Psalter commentary confirmed as printed-Amharic-book (not manuscript-only). Senkessar Abijā/Silä saint-dates route precise: Budge *Book of the Saints of the Ethiopian Church* vol. 2, Ṭǝr 21 + Ṭǝr 30 (≈ 29 Jan / 7 Feb Gregorian). Dating widened to Aksumite-to-Solomonic Ethiopian Christian range (4th-14th c. CE); precise composition date undetermined in current scholarship per Horovitz 1905 non-commitment. Three books: 1 Mq 36 chapters (Maqabis-of-Benjamin martyrology vs Ṣiruṣaydan); 2 Mq 21 chapters (Maqabis-of-Moab conversion + sons' martyrdom + Ṣiruṣaydan's death); 3 Mq 10 chapters (homiletic + angelological dialogue + Satan-refused-Adam tradition + resurrection-doctrine).
